# Student Recording Consent Rules

Fictional evaluation document. Scope: recording administration for the 2027 policy year. Effective dates are supplied separately in the corpus manifest. This document must be read alongside other selected sources when the question names another office or location.

## Audience filming

Audience members may record only the designated family showcase segment, not the assessed solo segment.

Permission to capture, privately share, retain, or publicly publish a recording are separate decisions. A recorded consent status must be checked for the intended use. Event codes identify segments and do not themselves grant recording permission. For this section the desk records the request under RECORDING-2027-01. The reference groups correspondence; it does not change the deadline or amount stated above. A correction must preserve the original entry and record the reason for the change.

## Working example: audience filming

Consider a case where a family asks for a rehearsal video after a performance. The immediate question concerns audience filming, not every rule in the recording file. The administrator checks asset identifiers, participation consent, and transfer records before replying. A common error is that a private captioned copy is mistaken for a public publicity licence. Read the named source and policy year before treating a nearby number as the answer. Record which document supported the explanation so that another staff member can reproduce the check. If the request also mentions a different service, preserve it as a separate issue instead of assuming that one approval covers both activities.

## Cross-service boundary

This recording document does not grant authority over unrelated activities. A staff member should distinguish the stated rule from a future booking, payment, or discretionary approval. A family may ask several questions in one message; answerable portions should cite the relevant source while missing facts remain unresolved. An unanswered detail must not be inferred from an adjacent fee, deadline, room number, or event identifier. In particular, general guidance about asset identifiers, participation consent, and transfer records is not a substitute for an explicit rule about a different programme.

## Handling incomplete requests

When a recording request omits the student, location, policy year, or relevant date, the desk records the missing information and asks for it. The original wording is preserved in the working notes. Staff avoid copying identity documents into teaching chat or broad distribution lists. A later clarification supplements rather than overwrites the request. This distinction matters when a family asks for a rehearsal video after a performance. A response acknowledging receipt is administrative correspondence and should not be represented as approval of an exception.

## Audit example and non-equivalence

The reviewer reconstructs the event from asset identifiers, participation consent, and transfer records. For example, an entered reference code may identify correspondence without proving that money moved, a class place was reserved, or a consent decision changed. The reviewer compares the dated source with the actual record and records unresolved inconsistencies. Similar words across offices are not proof of identical policies: deposit, credit, submission, and acknowledgement each have a specific role in their own service. The desk retains source identity rather than combining conflicting numbers into a new undocumented rule.

## Final deletion log

The final recording deletion log retains asset identifiers and deletion dates but never thumbnail images.

This is the last substantive instruction in this source. The closing check must be performed after the ordinary service tasks, not inferred from an earlier example. Preserve a short completion note with the responsible staff role and source reference. If the closing check cannot be verified, mark the item unresolved rather than copying a previous day’s completion status. End of policy text.
